content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "This judge text resolves D5 vs C5 by saying CR2 G answers the almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows while the sign's sense remains open, i.e., by row-level resolution rather than chain-against-chain footing.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "'never verse by verse' — one reading: it bars resolving the link by the judge's summary that individual rows were answered while the sign's sense stayed open; other reading: it only bars a bare stating-verse test and permits this shorthand.", "why": "The judge relies on CR2 G's answers to discrete almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows and the supposedly open sign-sense, rather than stating any chain-against-chain footing comparison required by K-C."}
